title.en: Too cold, warm enough, as good as
title.de: Zu, genug, so wie: too, enough, as … as
title.sl: Preveč, dovolj, tako kot: too, enough, as … as
title.it: Troppo, abbastanza, come: too, enough, as … as

goal.sl: Poveš, kdaj je česa preveč ali dovolj (too cold to swim, warm enough, too many sheep), kako zelo (a bit, quite, very) in kdaj je dvoje enako (as tall as Sam).
goal.de: Du sagst, wann etwas zu viel oder genug ist (too cold to swim, warm enough, too many sheep), wie sehr (a bit, quite, very) und wann zwei gleich sind (as tall as Sam).
goal.it: Dici quando qualcosa è troppo o abbastanza (too cold to swim, warm enough, too many sheep), quanto (a bit, quite, very) e quando due cose sono uguali (as tall as Sam).
goal.en: You can say when there is too much or enough (too cold to swim, warm enough, too many sheep), how much (a bit, quite, very) and when two things are the same (as tall as Sam).

say.sl: **too** (preveč) pove, da je več, kot hočeš, in da je to težava: **It's too cold.** (Prehladno je.) **This soup is too hot.** (Ta juha je prevroča.) **very** (zelo) je samo veliko: **It's very cold, but I like it.** (Zelo mrzlo je, a mi je všeč.)
say.de: **too** (zu) sagt, dass es mehr ist, als du willst, und dass das ein Problem ist: **It's too cold.** (Es ist zu kalt.) **This soup is too hot.** (Diese Suppe ist zu heiß.) **very** (sehr) ist nur viel: **It's very cold, but I like it.** (Es ist sehr kalt, aber mir gefällt es.)
say.it: **too** (troppo) dice che è più di quanto vuoi, e che è un problema: **It's too cold.** (Fa troppo freddo.) **This soup is too hot.** (Questa minestra è troppo calda.) **very** (molto) è solo tanto: **It's very cold, but I like it.** (Fa molto freddo, ma mi piace.)
say.en: **too** says it is more than you want, and that it's a problem: **It's too cold.** **This soup is too hot.** **very** only says a lot: **It's very cold, but I like it.**

examples.en: It's too cold. I'm going home.
examples.de: Es ist zu kalt. Ich gehe heim.
examples.it: Fa troppo freddo. Vado a casa.

examples.en: It's very cold, but I like it.
examples.sl: Zelo mrzlo je, a mi je všeč.
examples.de: Es ist sehr kalt, aber mir gefällt es.
examples.it: Fa molto freddo, ma mi piace.

say.sl: **enough** (dovolj) stoji za pridevnikom: **warm enough** (dovolj toplo), **big enough**. Pred samostalnikom: **enough water** (dovolj vode), **enough chairs**. Slovenščina ima pri pridevniku obratni red. **Is the water warm enough?** **We haven't got enough chairs.** (Nimamo dovolj stolov.)
say.de: **enough** (genug) steht nach dem Adjektiv: **warm enough** (warm genug), **big enough**. Vor dem Nomen: **enough water** (genug Wasser), **enough chairs**. Wie im Deutschen. **Is the water warm enough?** **We haven't got enough chairs.** (Wir haben nicht genug Stühle.)
say.it: **enough** (abbastanza) sta dopo l'aggettivo: **warm enough** (abbastanza caldo), **big enough**. Prima del nome: **enough water** (abbastanza acqua), **enough chairs**. Con l'aggettivo l'italiano ha l'ordine opposto. **Is the water warm enough?** **We haven't got enough chairs.** (Non abbiamo abbastanza sedie.)
say.en: **enough** stands after an adjective: **warm enough**, **big enough**. Before a noun: **enough water**, **enough chairs**. **Is the water warm enough?** **We haven't got enough chairs.**

examples.de: Der Lieferwagen ist nicht groß genug.
examples.it: Il furgone non è abbastanza grande.

say.sl: Naprej gre s **to** + osnovno obliko: **too cold to swim** (prehladno za plavanje), **warm enough to swim**, **old enough to drive**. Slovenski *za plavanje* ni *for swim*. S **for** gre oseba: **too big for me**, ali **-ing**: **too cold for swimming**. Oboje: **too heavy for me to carry**.
say.de: Weiter geht es mit **to** + Grundform: **too cold to swim** (zu kalt zum Schwimmen), **warm enough to swim**, **old enough to drive**. Nicht *for swim*. **for** nimmt eine Person: **too big for me**, oder **-ing**: **too cold for swimming**. Beides: **too heavy for me to carry**.
say.it: Si continua con **to** + la forma base: **too cold to swim** (troppo freddo per nuotare), **warm enough to swim**, **old enough to drive**. *per nuotare* non è *for swim*. **for** prende una persona: **too big for me**, o **-ing**: **too cold for swimming**. Tutti e due: **too heavy for me to carry**.
say.en: Go on with **to** + the base form: **too cold to swim**, **warm enough to swim**, **old enough to drive**. Not *for swim*. **for** takes a person: **too big for me**, or **-ing**: **too cold for swimming**. Both: **too heavy for me to carry**.

say.sl: **too much** gre s tem, kar se ne šteje: **too much salt** (preveč soli), **too much rain**. **too many** gre z množino: **too many sheep** (preveč ovc), **too many walkers**. Sam za glagolom: **You work too much.** **enough** je za oboje: **enough salt**, **enough sheep**.
say.de: **too much** geht mit dem, was man nicht zählt: **too much salt** (zu viel Salz), **too much rain**. **too many** geht mit dem Plural: **too many sheep** (zu viele Schafe), **too many walkers**. Allein nach dem Verb: **You work too much.** **enough** ist für beides: **enough salt**, **enough sheep**.
say.it: **too much** va con ciò che non si conta: **too much salt** (troppo sale), **too much rain**. **too many** va con il plurale: **too many sheep** (troppe pecore), **too many walkers**. Da solo dopo il verbo: **You work too much.** **enough** è per tutti e due: **enough salt**, **enough sheep**.
say.en: **too much** goes with what you can't count: **too much salt**, **too much rain**. **too many** goes with a plural: **too many sheep**, **too many walkers**. Alone after a verb: **You work too much.** **enough** is for both: **enough salt**, **enough sheep**.

examples.en: There's too much salt in the soup.
examples.de: In der Suppe ist zu viel Salz.

say.sl: Od malo do zelo: **a bit cold** (malo mrzlo), **quite cold** (kar mrzlo), **very cold**, **really cold**. V Britaniji je **quite** *kar*, v Ameriki pogosto *zelo*. Pred samostalnikom: **quite a long walk**, **a very long walk**. V govoru tudi **pretty cold**, tu na severu **right cold**, **dead good**: pravilno.
say.de: Von wenig bis sehr: **a bit cold** (ein bisschen kalt), **quite cold** (ziemlich kalt), **very cold**, **really cold**. Britisch ist **quite** *ziemlich*, amerikanisch oft *sehr*. Vor einem Nomen: **quite a long walk**, **a very long walk**. Gesprochen auch **pretty cold**, hier im Norden **right cold**, **dead good**: richtig.
say.it: Da poco a molto: **a bit cold** (un po' freddo), **quite cold** (abbastanza freddo), **very cold**, **really cold**. In Gran Bretagna **quite** è *abbastanza*, in America spesso *molto*. Davanti a un nome: **quite a long walk**, **a very long walk**. A voce anche **pretty cold**, qui al nord **right cold**, **dead good**: va bene.
say.en: From a little to a lot: **a bit cold**, **quite cold**, **very cold**, **really cold**. In Britain **quite** is fairly; in America it is often very. Before a noun: **quite a long walk**, **a very long walk**. In talk also **pretty cold**, and here in the North **right cold**, **dead good**: all right.

say.sl: **as … as** pove, da je enako: **Jack is as tall as Sam.** (Jack je tako visok kot Sam.) Za *tako … kot* je dvakrat **as**, ne *than*. **not as … as** pove manj: **The mill isn't as old as the inn.** = **The inn is older than the mill.** V govoru **as tall as me**, v pisavi tudi **as tall as I am**.
say.de: **as … as** sagt, dass es gleich ist: **Jack is as tall as Sam.** (Jack ist so groß wie Sam.) Für *so … wie* zweimal **as**, nicht *than*. **not as … as** sagt weniger: **The mill isn't as old as the inn.** = **The inn is older than the mill.** Gesprochen **as tall as me**, geschrieben auch **as tall as I am**.
say.it: **as … as** dice che è uguale: **Jack is as tall as Sam.** (Jack è alto come Sam.) Per *come* due volte **as**, non *than*. **not as … as** dice meno: **The mill isn't as old as the inn.** = **The inn is older than the mill.** A voce **as tall as me**, per iscritto anche **as tall as I am**.
say.en: **as … as** says they are the same: **Jack is as tall as Sam.** **as** both times, not *than*. **not as … as** says less: **The mill isn't as old as the inn.** = **The inn is older than the mill.** In talk **as tall as me**, in writing also **as tall as I am**.
